drhp.business: Maithan Alloys manufactures and exports manganese-based ferro alloys, including value-added manganese alloys, whose principal customers are steel manufacturers in India and overseas, as well as national and international suppliers of ferro alloys to steel makers. Besides manufacturing, the company carries on wholesale trading, and the Group has entered real estate, which remains substantially smaller than the core ferro alloy business. The company also runs a significant treasury and investment portfolio.

risks.note: The company names industry risk: slower product offtake, the cyclical steel industry, and unfair trade practices. Ferro alloy demand follows domestic and global steel production. In FY26, adverse market conditions partly suspended operations at the Kalyaneshwari unit.

Input-cost risk covers higher operating costs and volatile raw-material prices. Management cites pressure from swings in manganese ore prices and power costs, made worse in FY26 by an energy crisis that raised power, logistics and production costs. The Bobbili unit was shut from April 2023 because of a steep rise in power costs. Mitigants: PPAs with power utilities at pre-determined prices, and matching the order book to inventory.
risks.risk: Input cost: manganese ore and power

risks.note: The Directors' Report says escalating US tariffs, shifting supply chains, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the Middle East conflict disrupted global markets and trade routes. Export-import policies and global trade conditions are listed as industry factors.
Exchange-rate moves can hurt profitability. The company relies on a natural hedge by exporting more than it imports, and hedges when needed.
The company flags quality risk from inconsistent product quality and erratic quality of procured raw materials. It mitigates this with stringent inward and outward quality checks.
Congestion, strikes, channel blockages and storage, transport and handling risks. Plants sit close to downstream users and ports, which helps raw-material imports and product exports.

Strategic risk is the risk of wrong business decisions. It matters more as surplus funds move into equity markets and unlisted shares and the company diversifies into real estate. Management says it has been conservative on expansion and considers assets only at comfortable valuations.

Management says the decline in reported PAT must be read against the exceptionally high investment and other income of the preceding year. Surplus funds now go into equity capital markets and unlisted shares, so reported profit is exposed to market-linked investment returns.

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.

strategy.body:

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
